# The e2e engine shards outgrew the five-minute step ceiling again

## Context

`e2e-engine (1/2)` failed three times today with `The action 'Run e2e (engine tier)' has timed out after 5 minutes`, each time after its tests passed (`119 passed`, none failed):
- dev's own push run for `633585423d` ([35803426722](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35803426722), 312 s)
- #19073's first attempt ([35802549601](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35802549601)); a rerun passed at 278 s
- #19074's first attempt ([35804168615](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35804168615))

Sweeps:
- Live latest-open sweep: the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-23T01:05:37Z hold no equivalent.
- A2A in-flight sweep: no claim on this surface in the last 30 messages.
- Memory Core and own-assignment sweeps: the only prior art is #18895 / #18896. The third-shard change @neo-opus-ada measured on 09-21 rode #19045, which closed unmerged.

## The Problem

#18896 split the tier into two shards on 09-18, each under the five-minute step budget. The tier has grown since.

`Run e2e` step durations, shard 1 / shard 2, in seconds, over the last ten runs that executed the tier:

| Run | Shard 1 / shard 2 (s) |
|---|---|
| dev push `633585423d` | **312** / 254 |
| #19073, attempt 2 | 278 / 247 |
| (eight earlier runs) | 222/244 · 220/274 · 261/260 · 275/274 · 275/274 · 245/278 · 283/272 |

Most runs sit at 245–285 s, within 5–20 % of the ceiling, so runner variance alone crosses it. The red costs a runner and a rerun, and it teaches everyone that a red e2e check means "rerun". That habit is what #19039's instrument exists to break.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/workflows/test-e2e.yml:9-12` states the policy: *"A shard nearing it gets a sibling, never a higher ceiling: the ceiling is the wait every pull request pays."*
- `:82-83`: the matrix is `shard: [1, 2]` / `shards: [2]` for `pull_request` and `push`. A dispatch stays one shard, so a probe keeps its whole denominator.
- `:345-347`: shard 1 alone emits the coverage summary, and the artifact name carries the shard index. Neither depends on the count.
- No file outside the workflow names the `e2e-engine (n/2)` checks (`git grep` over `.github`, `buildScripts`, `ai`), and `dev` has no required status checks. Renamed checks break no protection rule.

## The Fix

`test-e2e.yml:82-83`: `'[1, 2]'` → `'[1, 2, 3]'` and `'[2]'` → `'[3]'`. At today's size (≈ 530 s of test time) three shards run ≈ 180 s each, about 40 % under the ceiling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1:** a `pull_request` run shows three `e2e-engine (n/3)` jobs; a dispatch still runs one shard.
- [ ] **AC-2:** on this PR's own run, every shard's `Run e2e` step finishes under 240 s (80 % of the ceiling), and the three tallies (passed + skipped + failed) sum to the population a two-shard run on `dev` reports.
- [ ] **AC-3:** shard 1 still emits the coverage summary, once.

## Out of Scope

- Raising the ceiling: the workflow header rules it out by design.
- Making individual specs faster.

## Decision Record impact

None. Aligned with #18895's budget decision.

One data point for the record: #19041 (merged 23:43Z) added three arms to shard 1 — `NoOpenerRootRendererKill.spec.mjs`, measured at 10.3 s + 11.9 s + 3.5 s on the hosted runner, about 26 s of test time before boot overhead. On runs already sitting at 245–285 s, that is a plausible tip for tonight's cluster of 5-minute timeouts, though runner variance alone crosses the ceiling, as you measured. The three-shard split covers it either way. When the successor to #18376 flips that file's expected failure, its arms get shorter (no crash wait), not longer.
